confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear session hijacking event followed by unauthorized cross-departmental data exfiltration. The mid-session IP change for the same session_id is a definitive indicator of hijacking.

attack_chain.description: User_08 logs in successfully from their normal IP (192.168.1.108).
User_08 performs legitimate file reads within their own department (/data/legal/).
Session hijacking occurs: The same session_id (sess_user_08_20260410_001) is used from a new, external IP (91.219.236.222), and the user begins accessing files in the HR department.
The attacker begins exfiltrating data from multiple departments including Finance, Security, Project Beta, and Marketing.
The attacker logs out from the hijacked session.

gaps: Information regarding the origin/reputation of IP 91.219.236.222.
Logs from the authentication provider to determine how the session token was intercepted (e.g., cookie theft, man-in-the-middle).
narrative: A security incident occurred involving the hijacking of user_08's session. After an initial legitimate login from a known IP, the session was hijacked by an external IP (91.219.236.222), which was then used to perform unauthorized cross-departmental file downloads across HR, Finance, Security, and Marketing departments.
